name: Old Captain Brisk
conversations: Ahoy. I sailed the sky-currents forty years, from Barkton to the edge of the clouds.
Now the currents have stopped. A sailor with no wind is just a man sitting on a bench.
See that cliff? That's where the Great Gust came from, every morning, regular as tea.
It's tied itself in a knot up there. Like a rope left in a sea-chest too long. Something's got to untangle it.
My old crew sang a shanty about the Tree. 'Give her breath and she'll give you joy.'
Funny. I always thought it was just a song.
Don't mind me, I'm just watching. A sailor knows: the wind always comes back.
